title: Why LEP Patients Miss FQHC Sliding Fee Access
summary: Learn where language barriers disrupt FQHC sliding fee discount enrollment, from screening and income review to document collection.
body_markdown:
###


It is a health center program that adjusts charges based on a patient's ability to pay. HRSA requires eligibility to be based on income and family size, with discounts for eligible patients at or below 200 percent of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.


###


Yes. HRSA requires health centers to have mechanisms for informing patients that sliding fee discounts are available and how to apply. HRSA gives examples that include intake materials, signage, websites, and information presented in languages and literacy levels appropriate for the patient population.


###


Patients can drop out at several points: awareness, screening, income questions, document collection, fee explanation, or recertification. A translated application alone does not cover those live conversations.


###


Track screening, application starts, completed eligibility reviews, document return, enrollment time, recertification, and interpreter use by preferred language. Look for steps where one language group drops off more often.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can provide immediate spoken-language support for registration, eligibility screening, document questions, phone follow-up, and recertification when it is part of the FQHC's approved language-access workflow.
